cards.a: Redundancy design is the disciplined selection of HA mechanisms matched to a business availability target, layering device, chassis, link, gateway, and path redundancy so every critical path has a backup and no single point of failure.

cards.q: What are the layers in a comprehensive HA design?
cards.a: Device/software (SSO, NSF, ISSU), chassis (redundant supervisors), link (EtherChannel/M-LAG), gateway (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP), path (ECMP, routing, multihoming), and power/cooling redundancy.

cards.q: What is the most important best practice in redundancy design?
cards.a: The top best practice is having no single point of failure on any critical path, supported by fast convergence, testing failovers, and consistent software across peers.

cards.q: Why is redundant not always equal to load-shared?
cards.a: Paired devices in an active/standby design protect against failure but do not split load, so redundancy should not be assumed to also provide load sharing.

cards.q: Why are bundled links preferred over single redundant links?
cards.a: EtherChannel bundles parallel links into one logical channel that STP does not block, so you get both redundancy and full utilization instead of one blocking link.

cards.q: What mechanisms cover gateway and path redundancy together?
cards.a: FHRP protocols such as HSRP, VRRP, and GLBP cover the first-hop gateway, while routing failover, ECMP, and BGP multihoming cover path and transit failures.

cards.q: What is a common design pattern at the distribution layer?
cards.a: A distribution layer often uses VSS or a switch stack with SSO to provide fast Layer 2 failover and a single management domain.

cards.q: Which commands verify the HA mechanisms?
cards.a: show redundancy states, show redundancy sso, show standby brief, show etherchannel summary, show ip route, show switch, and show vss.

cards.q: A failover causes dropped traffic and slow recovery; what is likely missing?
cards.a: SSO and NSF may not be enabled, so control state is not synchronized and forwarding stops during switchover; verify with show redundancy and the routing protocol NSF configuration.

cards.q: What is the key exam principle of layered HA design?
cards.a: No single mechanism covers all failures; HA is layered (device, chassis, link, gateway, path), and one mechanism such as SSO does not replace link or gateway redundancy.

cards.q: What is the redundancy design quick-review summary?
cards.a: Design with layered redundancy plus no single point of failure, using SSO/NSF for device, redundant supervisors for chassis, EtherChannel for links, HSRP/VRRP/GLBP for gateway, and routing/ECMP for path, while testing failover.
